scenarios.title: The Midnight Sweep
scenarios.clientName: Riverside dwellers of the flood-belt settlement (347 households)
scenarios.bench: Constitutional chamber seized of an urgent public-interest challenge
scenarios.factualBackground: At 2:10 a.m., a demolition column with police escort levelled 347 informal homes along a storm canal. No notice preceded the operation, two decades of domicile records were confiscated in the rubble, and no rehabilitation scheme exists. The municipality invokes flood-safety bylaws and an ex parte order obtained in its own proceedings. Families are living in the open beside the debris of their homes.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether summary nocturnal demolition without notice, hearing or resettlement violates the right to life and shelter, and what restitution the court must order.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Standing Counsel for the Municipal Authority
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: My Lords, this was a statutory flood-control operation under a subsisting order. The structures occupied the canal buffer in patent violation of building by-laws; twenty years of occupancy is twenty years of constructive notice. A midnight execution injures nobody who obeyed the law. The petitioners are trespassers seeking a subsidy in the guise of a fundamental right.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Locus standi of the displaced; finality of the municipal demolition order; the flood-safety justification.

scenarios.closingPrompt: The Bench rises for the last time in this matter. Frame the operative order: restitution, rehabilitation, and the precedent this record should leave behind.

scenarios.title: The Interrogation Room
scenarios.clientName: A suspect charged on the strength of an unwarned confession
scenarios.bench: State supreme court, criminal division, hearing a suppression appeal
scenarios.factualBackground: Detectives questioned the accused for six hours in a locked interview room. No warning of the right to silence or counsel was given; the accused asked twice whether he could leave and was told the interview would end 'when you tell us the truth.' A signed statement followed. The prosecution's entire case rests on that statement and on a torn shirt recovered from his apartment.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether the unwarned custodial statement and its fruits must be suppressed, and whether the interrogation's length and tone compounded the violation.

opposingCounselPersona.name: State Deputy Attorney General
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: Your Honor, this was a voluntary interview with a willing participant. The warnings regime is a procedural trinket, not a constitutional straitjacket; the statement was reliable, the shirt was corroborative, and the public interest in convicting the guilty should not be felled by a tree of paper. Suppression is a remedy for tyrants, not for detectives doing their jobs.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Voluntariness on the facts; the attenuation doctrine; harmless-error arguments over the shirt.

scenarios.closingPrompt: Final argument. The appellate panel wants a rule it can apply to every interrogation room in the State. Give it one.

scenarios.title: The Frozen Transfers
scenarios.clientName: A European health-data cooperative serving 2.4 million patients
scenarios.bench: EU referencing chamber on a cross-border data-processing referral
scenarios.factualBackground: A data-processing agreement routes patient records to a third country whose intelligence statutes compel disclosure on demand and criminalise the recipient's silence about it. The importer's own transparency reports admit state access without judicial oversight. The cooperative suspended transfers after its supervisory authority opened an inquiry; processors and hospital clients now demand restoration or a lawful alternative framework.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether transfers may lawfully continue under contractual safeguards alone, what verification the exporter owes, and whether the receiving country's surveillance regime defeats adequacy.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Counsel for the Cloud Processor
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: Mr President, standard contractual clauses remain the Commission-approved transfer tool. The third country's laws are for that country's courts; the exporter's obligation is a paper audit, not a geopolitical veto. Suspending transfers will fragment patient care across Europe within a fortnight — the Court should weigh lives, not letters of the law.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Standing of the cooperative; the sufficiency of contractual verification; the proportionality of a total transfer ban.

scenarios.closingPrompt: The referral closes. Give the Court the precise test a thousand exporters will apply tomorrow morning.

scenarios.title: The Thirty-Month Trial
scenarios.clientName: An accused whose trial clock ran well past every ceiling
scenarios.bench: Appellate chamber on an application for a stay for delay
scenarios.factualBackground: The accused was charged with impaired driving causing bodily harm. The trial took 31 months to reach completion: 11 months of pre-commitment scheduling failures, 9 months consumed by a duplicate disclosure exercise, and two adjournments attributed to court-availability. The Crown concedes the arithmetic but attributes 14 months to a province-wide judicial shortage it calls 'exceptional circumstances.'
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether the net delay presumptively violates the reasonable-time guarantee, whether the systemic-shortage exception applies, and what remedy follows.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Crown Appellate Counsel
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: My Lords, the framework was never meant to release every case that brushes a ceiling. The accused contributed no pushback, the delay was largely institutional, and the transitional exception exists precisely for this: a court system in crisis cannot be permitted to become a get-out-of-jail instrument. Society's interest in adjudication on the merits must count for something.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Clear-case exception; the accused's failure to raise delay earlier; the societal-interest balancing.

scenarios.closingPrompt: The application closes. Articulate the rule the trial courts of this province will pin above their calendars.

scenarios.title: The Bottle on the Shelf
scenarios.clientName: A supermarket chain prosecuted for a self-service restricted sale
scenarios.bench: Court of Appeal on a case stated from a magistrates' conviction
scenarios.factualBackground: A statutory-restricted medicine was displayed on an open self-service shelf. A customer selected a box, walked to the till, and the assistant — a trainee on her second shift — rang it up without asking for the supervising pharmacist. The enforcement authority prosecuted the store for contravening the sale restriction. The magistrates convicted, reasoning that the store 'offered' the product the moment it hit the shelf.
scenarios.coreDispute: Where a self-service sale legally concludes — at shelf or at till — and whether the store's display can constitute the prohibited 'sale' at all.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Counsel for the Enforcement Authority
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: My Lords, the store engineered the shelf to make the customer's hand the shop's hand. Every retail-chain format in the country funnels goods to a till; if that is not an offer of the product, supervision dies at the stockroom door. The conviction should stand to keep every restricted sale in the country under a pharmacist's eye.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: The statutory purpose of supervision; 'sale' construed broadly; the store's operational control over the display.

scenarios.closingPrompt: Final submission. Decide where the law of the shop floor ends and the law of the contract begins.

scenarios.title: The Lands That Never Emptied
scenarios.clientName: Traditional owners of the granite-river country
scenarios.factualBackground: Three pastoral leases were granted over granite-river country between 1915 and 1963. The claimant group has maintained continuous ceremonial and foraging connection; the leases were never fenced, never resided on by lessees, and were used exclusively for incidental grazing. The State contends any grant extinguished traditional rights absolutely; the pastoralists concede non-exclusive use but claim primacy in any conflict.
scenarios.coreDispute: Whether historical pastoral leases extinguished native title absolutely, or whether the two systems of rights can coexist with the lease prevailing only on inconsistency.

opposingCounselPersona.name: Counsel for the State and the Pastoral Interests
opposingCounselPersona.initialOpeningStatement: Your Honours, the grants created estates in land of a known quality; the law of real property does not do partial extinguishment. Every subsequent development — mortgages, water licences, the lot — presumes exclusivity. To find coexistence now is to inject uncertainty into every leasehold in the State and unsettle the registered assumptions of a century.
opposingCounselPersona.interlocutoryAttackTheme: Certainty of title; the legal character of pastoral leases; the continuity of traditional connection evidence.

scenarios.closingPrompt: The determination awaits. Close on what the common law owes to a system of law it once refused to see.
